articles.title: Codes and messages you may meet, and what they mean
articles.body:
This table lists codes that appear in the platform's documentation. If you meet a code that is not here, copy it exactly, do not guess, and ask your manager.

| Code | Where you meet it | What it means | What to do |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `UNKNOWN` | A payment status | We do not know whether money moved. | [[a:b07-03]] |
| `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | Error classification | A customer or merchant limit was reached. | Explain the limit; do not retry in a loop. |
| `RETRYABLE_OTP` | Error classification | The customer typed a wrong code and may try again. | Nothing; three tries by default. |
| `TERMINAL_DECLINE` | Error classification | A final refusal by the partner. | Nothing; the payment failed. |
| `GATEWAY_FAULT` | Error classification | The partner is broken. Counts toward the circuit breaker. | [[a:b10-02]] |
| `AMBIGUOUS` | Error classification | We cannot tell what happened. Treated as `UNKNOWN` on money steps. | [[a:b07-03]] |
| `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` | Customer-facing reason | The customer's account did not have enough. | Tell the customer to use another method. |
| `LINK_NOT_AVAILABLE` | Starting a payment | The link expired, was cancelled or has no free slot. | Merchant creates a new link, or wait if a payment is in progress. |
| `VALIDATION_FAILED` | Back Office or portal request | The request shape was wrong (for example a field name). | Report with the screen; do not retry blindly. |
| `SCHEMA_INVALID` | AI import check | The spec file has the wrong shape. | Use the repair message ([[a:b06-14]]). |
| `STEP_TYPE_NOT_IMPORTABLE` | AI import check | A step type must be added in the wizard instead. | [[a:b06-14]] |
| `INVALID_ATTEMPT_TRANSITION` | Engine log | An event tried an illegal state change. | Report to Engineering. |
| `FORBIDDEN_SERVICE_IDENTITY` | Core log | A service used the wrong certificate or channel. | Security Admin. |
| `403` | Any screen | The core refused: role, authority or the two-person rule. | [[a:b03-07]] |
| `401` | Any screen | Not signed in or session ended. | Sign in again. |
| `409` | Partner answer | A conflict (for example the same request body changed). | Gateway Admin. |
| `422` | Partner answer | The partner rejected the data (for example a duplicate reference). | Gateway Admin. |
| `429` | Partner answer | Too many requests too quickly. | Do not retry in a loop. |
| `500` | Any answer | The other side broke. On a money step this becomes `UNKNOWN`. | [[a:b07-03]] |

articles.title: About this guide: version, updates and the Academy
articles.body:
* Every build of the guide has a **content version**. Your reading progress records the version you read, so a major change can ask you to read again.
* The guide explains **rules, not records**. It contains no live data, no real thresholds, no names and no secrets.
* If the guide and the screen disagree, **stop and ask**; use **Report a problem** on the article.
* Some features exist in the design but have no screen yet. Those articles show a banner. See [[a:b03-08]].
* The **Employee Academy** teaches the same material as lessons, practice labs and exams. Your progress is shared between the Guide and the Academy.
* The Merchant Guide and the Checkout Help are separate documents for other audiences.

Late-confirmation grace (default) 24 hours
Webhook timestamp tolerance 5 minutes
Webhook duplicate memory 7 days
Approval request lifetime 7 days
Emergency suspension ratification 24 hours
Join request inactive expiry 30 days
Join review deadline 2 business days (LOW/STANDARD), 5 (HIGH)
Beneficial owner threshold (default) 25%
AML case deadlines (default) CRITICAL 4 h, HIGH 1 day, MEDIUM 3 days, LOW 5 days
POS screen idle limit 15 minutes
Outbound call limits 10 s (auth, status), 15 s (start, confirm, refund)
Maximum response size 2 MB
Retention (default) 5 years after the relationship ends
KYB refresh HIGH yearly, STANDARD 2 years, LOW 3 years
Document expiry notices 30 and 7 days before
Go-live gates 12
Automatic sandbox scenarios 15
Database tables 64
Edge cases catalogued 140

glossary.short: A change of numbers that a trusted record-keeper agrees to: money leaves the payer's account and arrives in the receiver's.
The person who pays. Anonymous on our platform; they never sign in.
A business that we checked and allowed to take payments.
One place where a merchant takes payments (a website, an app, a branch). Linked to exactly one wallet.
A merchant's balance on our books. A number we owe the merchant, calculated from the ledger, not a bank account.
A request to pay one fixed amount, with a secret key. Single-use or multi-use.
The in-shop counter. A terminal is the place; a screen is a display paired to it.
A secret string (starting `pg_live_`) that lets a merchant's software create links. Shown once.
The Libyan dinar. 1 LYD = 1000 dirhams, so amounts have three decimals.
One thousandth of a dinar.
The multiplier used to write an amount for a partner (1, 100 or 1000). A wrong scale makes an amount 1000 times wrong.
Cutting extra decimals: nearest, up, down, or none.
What we charge the merchant. Our revenue.
What the payment company charges us. Our cost.
Who effectively pays our commission: the merchant absorbs it, the payer pays a surcharge, or it is split.
Commission minus gateway fee.
One technical door to one payment company: its addresses, login, steps and how to read its answers.
A shared network that connects many banks and wallets. In Libya, Moamalat runs the national card switch.
A company offering one door to many payment methods. One more company in the money path.
What the customer sees and picks (for example Sadad). Has a form, limits and logo.
The link between a rail and a gateway through a credential policy, with priority, cost, limits and health.
The secret identifiers for one gateway in one environment, owned by the platform or by a merchant.
Where the money lands: platform clearing, merchant direct, or provider held.
How the customer completes a payment: OTP, redirect, embedded, push, QR, pay code, deep link, manual, or hybrid.
A code valid once for a short time, usually sent by SMS.
Sending the customer to the payment company's own page and back.
A rail that offers several collection modes at once.
A square code scanned by a bank or wallet app to start a payment.
The customer taps Approve in their wallet app.
The menu and rules for asking a computer system to do things.
A message sent and the answer received.
A computer that waits for requests and answers them.
A payment company phoning us to say something happened.
Where every incoming message is stored first, exactly as received, and never deleted.
Asking again and again whether something is ready.
One read-only question to a partner about one payment. The safest way to learn the truth.
A request is idempotent if sending it twice has the effect of once.
Repeating a request. Forbidden for money steps.
No answer within the time limit. On a money step it makes a payment unknown.
A text format for data, like `{"amount":"10.50"}`.
A path such as `result.transaction_id` that picks one value out of an answer.
A practice world where nothing real moves.
The real world: real money, real customers.
Our internal service that imitates payment companies for drills. Never in production.
One try to pay a link, with its own state, references and pinned configuration.
One of 14 states of an attempt (for example `UNKNOWN`, `SUCCEEDED`).
We do not know whether money moved. Never guess; use Inquire.
Our unique number for a payment. Quote it, never the customer's name.
A reservation on a link taken before a payment starts, so one invoice cannot be paid twice.
The version of settings an attempt started with. Later edits do not change it.
When a payment stops waiting. The smaller of the partner's and the platform's limit.
Time after expiry in which a late confirmation is still accepted.
A confirmation arriving after the payment expired or failed.
The step that completes a payment. Never retried automatically.
A browser or return-address message that makes us ask the partner; it never proves payment.
Success checked by our server on five facts: status, reference, amount, currency and environment.
Our standard five-word vocabulary for a partner's answers.
Maps a partner answer to a canonical status. First match wins.
Gives a partner's error code a classification and customer message.
Automatically hides a failing route and moves traffic to the next one.
A task created by the system when a payment or statement needs a human.
The recipe for one phase of a gateway: an ordered list of steps.
One of ten parts of a gateway recipe, such as INITIATE, SUBMIT or VERIFY.
One action inside a phase: call a web address, compute a value, render something.
A small safe operation applied to a value, from a closed library.
Cleans what a customer types (for example Arabic digits) before checking it.
One input of a rail's customer form.
How carefully a field is treated: normal, sensitive or full card number.
The full card number. Kept in memory only for one call.
A recipe for signing or checking messages.
A seal proving a message came from someone who knows a shared secret and was not changed.
A fingerprint of data: same data, same fingerprint; cannot be reversed.
Locking data so only someone with the key can read it.
Anything that proves identity: passwords, keys, tokens, certificate keys. Write-only on this platform.
A secret you can replace but never read back.
Both sides show a digital ID card. Used between our own services.
A digital ID card issued by an authority we trust.
Changing a secret on schedule or after a leak, with an overlap period.
An attack that makes our server call addresses it should not. Blocked by the engine.
One of the engine protections against mistakes and attacks.
An immutable snapshot of a gateway's configuration.
The twelve checks every version must pass before going live.
Returning to an earlier version.
Starting a new version with a small share of traffic.
How well a gateway's behaviour is known.
The rule deciding which payment methods a customer sees.
The person who proposes a sensitive change.
The different person who decides it.
One proposes, another decides. Never the same person.
The record of a proposed change, its reason, its diff and its decision.
What would change, old value to new value.
A field whose change needs two people.
A harmless field edited directly and logged.
Second-person confirmation, within 24 hours, of an emergency action.
Risk-reducing actions may be immediate; risk-increasing or money-moving ones need approval first.
A specific permission on an account. No authorities means no access.
A job family, such as FINANCE or OPERATOR.
The unchangeable record of who did what, when.
Old and new value of every changed field.
All journal entries: our accounting books. Append-only.
Writing both sides of every movement so they must match.
One page of the ledger describing one event.
One row: an account, a direction and an amount.
One of two directions of a line. Not "bad".
The other direction.
A named place where an amount is tracked. There are 11 kinds.
Our real money.
Money a partner holds for us but has not paid yet.
Money that arrived but does not clearly belong yet.
Money held while compliance decides.
Money set aside while a dispute is open.
The equation that must always hold; the difference is the drift.
The partner paying us collected money, usually days later.
Matching a partner's statement to our books.
Any non-standard money movement; always two people.
A merchant's request to be paid its balance into its bank.
Returning money to the payer.
A payer or its bank taking money back through the card or payment network.
A case that a payment should be returned.
A partner's file listing what it processed.
Offsetting what two sides owe each other.
Checking that a business is real before allowing it.
The record of one onboarding attempt.
The deadline attached to a case or review.
A real person who owns 25% or more, or controls, a business.
LOW, STANDARD or HIGH: how risky a merchant is judged to be.
Rules and activities that stop criminals hiding the origin of money.
Comparing names against official and internal lists.
An official list of people, companies and countries we must not deal with.
Someone with a prominent public role. Allowed, but riskier.
Negative news about a person or business.
A name resembling a listed name. A person must decide.
A possible match decided to be a different person.
A limit on how often or how much within a time window.
A declarative pattern or amount rule that can hold money or open a case.
Splitting amounts to stay under a threshold.
A review of a suspected issue, with severity, deadline and decision.
The senior owner of suspicious-activity decisions.
A report to the authority about suspicious activity.
Telling someone they are under suspicion. Forbidden.
Data only Compliance, the MLRO and audit may see.
The Central Bank of Libya, our regulator.
How long records must be kept.
A second proof of identity, usually a six-digit code sent by SMS to your registered phone.
Tricking a person into giving away secrets or acting wrongly.
A step-by-step procedure for a known incident.
Anything threatening money, customers or trust.
A safe queue that ensures a message is sent once.
An SMS, e-mail or in-app message about an event.
The JSON file an AI drafts for the Smart AI Integration.
A sample request and answer used to check a result offline.

cards.title: Approve a request from another person
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are approving a change proposed by someone else. Approving also **executes** the change immediately.

**Check first**
- [ ] I opened **Details** and read the old value and the new value.
- [ ] I understand what this will change, and can say it in one sentence.
- [ ] The merchant name, amount and currency are the ones I expect.
- [ ] The maker's reason makes sense and is more than "ok".
- [ ] I am not the maker, and nobody asked me to approve without reading.
- [ ] The environment badge is correct (`SANDBOX` or `LIVE`).

**Never**
- Never approve something you cannot explain.
- Never approve because someone is waiting or in a hurry.
- Never approve on the strength of a phone call or chat message.

**If you made a mistake**
Tell your manager and the owner of the area at once. A change that was executed is corrected by a new approved change, not by editing. See [[a:b10-09]].
checklist: I opened **Details** and read the old value and the new value.
I understand what this will change, and can say it in one sentence.
The merchant name, amount and currency are the ones I expect.
The maker's reason makes sense and is more than "ok".
I am not the maker, and nobody asked me to approve without reading.
The environment badge is correct (`SANDBOX` or `LIVE`).

cards.title: Reject a request
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are refusing a proposed change. The maker will see your **Decision Reason** and may re-draft.

**Check first**
- [ ] I wrote a real reason: what I checked and why I refused.
- [ ] My reason contains no password, code or confidential detail.
- [ ] The reason does not mention AML or screening if a merchant could read it.
- [ ] I checked that this is the right request, not a similar one.

**Never**
- Never reject with "no" or "ok".
- Never reject to punish or to avoid work.

**If you made a mistake**
The maker can create a new request. If you rejected the wrong one, tell the maker straight away so they re-submit.
checklist: I wrote a real reason: what I checked and why I refused.
My reason contains no password, code or confidential detail.
The reason does not mention AML or screening if a merchant could read it.
I checked that this is the right request, not a similar one.

cards.title: Propose an adjustment
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are proposing a money movement: a refund, a chargeback, a manual credit or debit, or a correction. A different Finance user must approve it.

**Check first**
- [ ] I found the original payment by its **reference**.
- [ ] The amount does not exceed the original payment, and the currency is the same.
- [ ] I chose the correct type and the correct account.
- [ ] I decided deliberately whether the commission is reversed.
- [ ] I checked whether a dispute already covers this payment, so money is not returned twice.
- [ ] My reason says what I checked, what I found and why ([[a:b04-06]]).

**Never**
- Never propose from a screenshot, phone call or chat alone.
- Never split one adjustment into several to avoid review.

**If you made a mistake**
If it is still pending, withdraw it. If it was executed, propose an offsetting adjustment with **Reverse**. Never edit an executed adjustment.
checklist: I found the original payment by its **reference**.
The amount does not exceed the original payment, and the currency is the same.
I chose the correct type and the correct account.
I decided deliberately whether the commission is reversed.
I checked whether a dispute already covers this payment, so money is not returned twice.
My reason says what I checked, what I found and why ([[a:b04-06]]).

cards.title: Reverse an adjustment
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are proposing a new adjustment that cancels the effect of an earlier one. The earlier one stays in the books.

**Check first**
- [ ] I confirmed the earlier adjustment is the wrong one, by reading its details.
- [ ] I understand the money will move in the opposite direction.
- [ ] I wrote the reason, including what went wrong the first time.
- [ ] The merchant name, amount and currency match the earlier adjustment.

**Never**
- Never reverse to hide a mistake without telling your manager.
- Never reverse the same adjustment twice.

**If you made a mistake**
Withdraw the pending reversal if it is wrong, and tell Finance. See [[a:b08-08]].
checklist: I confirmed the earlier adjustment is the wrong one, by reading its details.
I understand the money will move in the opposite direction.
I wrote the reason, including what went wrong the first time.
The merchant name, amount and currency match the earlier adjustment.

cards.title: Process or approve a cash-out
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are starting or finalising a payout of a merchant's balance to a real bank account. It cannot be undone by the platform.

**Check first**
- [ ] The destination is the merchant's verified bank account in its legal name (check the snapshot).
- [ ] The merchant is `ACTIVE`: not suspended, no negative balance, no hold.
- [ ] The amount is no more than the wallet balance.
- [ ] The ledger invariant shows zero drift and payouts are not halted.
- [ ] I am not the person who made the bank transfer (for the final approval).
- [ ] I read the amount aloud once: the figure, the merchant and the bank.

**Never**
- Never change the bank details yourself.
- Never process because a merchant phoned and said it is urgent.
- Never approve and execute your own processing.

**If you made a mistake**
Tell your manager and the Security Admin immediately. If a wrong transfer was made at the bank, contact the bank at once. Books are corrected by approved adjustments.
checklist: The destination is the merchant's verified bank account in its legal name (check the snapshot).
The merchant is `ACTIVE`: not suspended, no negative balance, no hold.
The amount is no more than the wallet balance.
The ledger invariant shows zero drift and payouts are not halted.
I am not the person who made the bank transfer (for the final approval).
I read the amount aloud once: the figure, the merchant and the bank.

cards.title: Reject a cash-out
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are refusing a payout request. Nothing has been subtracted from the wallet yet.

**Check first**
- [ ] I wrote the reason clearly.
- [ ] I checked the reason does not reveal AML or screening matters.
- [ ] I told or will tell the merchant only a generic reason.

**Never**
- Never reject for an AML reason in words the merchant could read.

**If you made a mistake**
The merchant can request again. If rejected by mistake, tell Finance so it is re-handled.
checklist: I wrote the reason clearly.
I checked the reason does not reveal AML or screening matters.
I told or will tell the merchant only a generic reason.

cards.title: Resolve an UNKNOWN payment by hand
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are deciding that an uncertain payment **succeeded** or **failed**. This credits money or frees a link, and it needs a second person.

**Check first**
- [ ] I pressed **Inquire** and read the answer in the step log.
- [ ] I have **evidence from the partner**: a statement line or a written reply naming our reference or the provider reference.
- [ ] The amount and currency in the evidence match the attempt.
- [ ] The environment is `LIVE` and this is the right attempt.
- [ ] My reason names the evidence ([[a:b04-06]]).

**Never**
- Never resolve because it is old.
- Never resolve from a customer's screenshot or phone call.
- Never ask the customer to pay again.

**If you made a mistake**
Tell your manager and Finance. A wrongly credited payment or a wrongly failed one is corrected by a new approved adjustment. See [[a:b07-03]].
checklist: I pressed **Inquire** and read the answer in the step log.
I have **evidence from the partner**: a statement line or a written reply naming our reference or the provider reference.
The amount and currency in the evidence match the attempt.
The environment is `LIVE` and this is the right attempt.
My reason names the evidence ([[a:b04-06]]).

cards.title: Release a link reservation
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are freeing the slot held by an uncertain payment so that the link can be used again.

**Check first**
- [ ] I have evidence that **no money moved** for this attempt.
- [ ] I understand the customer could still pay twice if I am wrong.
- [ ] The case notes explain the evidence.

**Never**
- Never release while the partner might still confirm.
- Never release to satisfy an impatient merchant.

**If you made a mistake**
If the customer paid again, handle the second payment as an overpayment through Finance ([[a:b07-08]]) and tell your manager.
checklist: I have evidence that **no money moved** for this attempt.
I understand the customer could still pay twice if I am wrong.
The case notes explain the evidence.

cards.title: Run a bulk inquiry
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are asking a partner about many payments at once. It sends many calls and may be rate-limited.

**Check first**
- [ ] I limited it to the affected route and time window.
- [ ] The partner is up (not in an open circuit-breaker period).
- [ ] I am not repeating a bulk inquiry I just ran.
- [ ] The environment is correct.

**Never**
- Never run it against all routes "just in case".
- Never run it while the partner is down.

**If you made a mistake**
Stop and tell the Gateway Admin if the partner starts refusing calls.
checklist: I limited it to the affected route and time window.
The partner is up (not in an open circuit-breaker period).
I am not repeating a bulk inquiry I just ran.
The environment is correct.

cards.title: Approve a join request
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are approving a business to take live payments. The merchant becomes active at once, or after a second reviewer if one is required.

**Check first**
- [ ] All seven checks are done and recorded.
- [ ] Screening is `CLEAR`, or a possible match was decided by Compliance.
- [ ] The payout account is in the merchant's legal name.
- [ ] The proposed risk tier is justified.
- [ ] No unresolved duplicate or related-party flag.
- [ ] I am not pressured by a deadline or a sales request.

**Never**
- Never approve with an incomplete checklist.
- Never discuss screening with the applicant.

**If you made a mistake**
Tell Compliance. An approved merchant can be suspended; a wrongly approved one is reviewed under [[a:b05-08]].
checklist: All seven checks are done and recorded.
Screening is `CLEAR`, or a possible match was decided by Compliance.
The payout account is in the merchant's legal name.
The proposed risk tier is justified.
No unresolved duplicate or related-party flag.
I am not pressured by a deadline or a sales request.

cards.title: Reject a join request
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are refusing an application. The applicant gets a neutral reason code and may apply again after correcting the cause.

**Check first**
- [ ] I chose the reason code that fits, knowing a revealing code will be shown as `POLICY`.
- [ ] My internal note states what I checked.
- [ ] I am not rejecting because of a screening result without Compliance involvement.

**Never**
- Never tell the applicant about screening.
- Never reject for a personal reason.

**If you made a mistake**
A wrongful rejection can be corrected by a new request linked to the old one. Tell your manager.
checklist: I chose the reason code that fits, knowing a revealing code will be shown as `POLICY`.
My internal note states what I checked.
I am not rejecting because of a screening result without Compliance involvement.

cards.title: Suspend a merchant
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are stopping a business from taking payments and cashing out. It takes effect now and must be ratified within 24 hours.

**Check first**
- [ ] Delay would cause harm (fraud, sanctions, expired documents, merchant request).
- [ ] I chose the correct reason code.
- [ ] I wrote the reason so a stranger can understand it.
- [ ] I know who will ratify it.
- [ ] I will not tell the merchant the real reason if it is AML.

**Never**
- Never suspend casually or as a bargaining tool.
- Never tell the merchant it is because of compliance.

**If you made a mistake**
Ask a `COMPLIANCE` or `MLRO` user to review immediately. Reinstatement needs prior approval.
checklist: Delay would cause harm (fraud, sanctions, expired documents, merchant request).
I chose the correct reason code.
I wrote the reason so a stranger can understand it.
I know who will ratify it.
I will not tell the merchant the real reason if it is AML.

cards.title: Reinstate a merchant
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are letting a suspended business take payments and cash out again. This increases risk, so a different Compliance or MLRO user must approve first.

**Check first**
- [ ] The reason for suspension is resolved and documented.
- [ ] Compliance agrees (without telling the merchant why it was restricted).
- [ ] Documents are current.
- [ ] No open case or hold is unresolved.

**Never**
- Never reinstate on a merchant's request alone.
- Never use the emergency path.

**If you made a mistake**
Suspend again if reinstated by mistake and tell Compliance.
checklist: The reason for suspension is resolved and documented.
Compliance agrees (without telling the merchant why it was restricted).
Documents are current.
No open case or hold is unresolved.

cards.title: Submit a sensitive merchant change
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are asking a second person to approve a change to a sensitive field such as payout bank details, tax ID or risk tier.

**Check first**
- [ ] The change was requested in the merchant's own portal or in writing, not by phone.
- [ ] The new bank account is in the merchant's legal name.
- [ ] Supporting documents are attached.
- [ ] I wrote the reason and the old and new values are correct.

**Never**
- Never edit payout details after a phone request.
- Never include secrets in the reason.

**If you made a mistake**
Withdraw the request before a checker acts. If executed wrongly, submit a corrective change and tell Security.
checklist: The change was requested in the merchant's own portal or in writing, not by phone.
The new bank account is in the merchant's legal name.
Supporting documents are attached.
I wrote the reason and the old and new values are correct.

cards.title: Propose an AML case resolution
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are proposing to release, void, freeze or escalate a case. The MLRO approves. Money moves only after approval.

**Check first**
- [ ] I reviewed all evidence and the rule that caused the case.
- [ ] My rationale states what I found and why the resolution is right.
- [ ] The rationale contains nothing a merchant could later read.
- [ ] I considered whether a report is required.
- [ ] I am not the checker.

**Never**
- Never tell the merchant or customer anything about the case.
- Never release to meet a deadline.

**If you made a mistake**
Withdraw before the MLRO acts. Tell the MLRO if you proposed in error.
checklist: I reviewed all evidence and the rule that caused the case.
My rationale states what I found and why the resolution is right.
The rationale contains nothing a merchant could later read.
I considered whether a report is required.
I am not the checker.

cards.title: Decide a screening match
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are deciding whether a possible name match is a false positive, a true match or needs escalation.

**Check first**
- [ ] I compared date of birth, nationality, ID and other attributes.
- [ ] I wrote the evidence for my decision.
- [ ] If I suppress future matches I set an expiry date.
- [ ] If it may be a sanctions match I will escalate, not decide alone.

**Never**
- Never mark a match false because the merchant is large or important.
- Never discuss the result outside Compliance.

**If you made a mistake**
Tell the MLRO immediately; a wrong disposition can be re-opened.
checklist: I compared date of birth, nationality, ID and other attributes.
I wrote the evidence for my decision.
If I suppress future matches I set an expiry date.
If it may be a sanctions match I will escalate, not decide alone.

cards.title: Create or change an AML rule
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are changing the rules that hold money and open cases. The MLRO must approve.

**Check first**
- [ ] I ran the dry-run and read how many holds and cases it would create.
- [ ] I know whether this tightens or loosens the rule.
- [ ] If loosening, I accept that it needs full review.
- [ ] The scope is correct.

**Never**
- Never loosen a rule to reduce workload.
- Never test on live.

**If you made a mistake**
Withdraw the proposal. If activated wrongly, propose the corrective change with the MLRO.
checklist: I ran the dry-run and read how many holds and cases it would create.
I know whether this tightens or loosens the rule.
If loosening, I accept that it needs full review.
The scope is correct.

cards.title: Create or save a regulatory report
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are drafting or saving a report to the authority. Once approved and submitted it is frozen.

**Check first**
- [ ] The reporting rule is `CONFIRMED`, not `PROVISIONAL`.
- [ ] Facts in the report match the case.
- [ ] The report is stored as confidential.
- [ ] No other system or person is told about it.

**Never**
- Never tell the subject.
- Never file from a provisional rule.

**If you made a mistake**
Corrections are new linked reports. Tell the MLRO.
checklist: The reporting rule is `CONFIRMED`, not `PROVISIONAL`.
Facts in the report match the case.
The report is stored as confidential.
No other system or person is told about it.

cards.title: Submit a gateway version for approval
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are asking a Security Admin to approve a configuration for live money.

**Check first**
- [ ] I read the compiled request preview and the amount pipeline results.
- [ ] The 15-scenario suite and contract tests are green.
- [ ] The money step cannot retry automatically.
- [ ] Every weak channel must ask the partner.
- [ ] I named a rollback version and a canary plan.
- [ ] I did not use a real secret in any example.

**Never**
- Never submit with a failing gate.
- Never skip reading the preview.

**If you made a mistake**
Withdraw the submission. If it went live badly, roll back to the named version and follow [[a:b10-02]].
checklist: I read the compiled request preview and the amount pipeline results.
The 15-scenario suite and contract tests are green.
The money step cannot retry automatically.
Every weak channel must ask the partner.
I named a rollback version and a canary plan.
I did not use a real secret in any example.

cards.title: Create or change a route
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are changing which payment methods customers see, how traffic is split and what fees apply.

**Check first**
- [ ] I know which rail and gateway this route joins.
- [ ] Minimum, maximum and daily cap are correct and in LYD.
- [ ] The credential policy and scope are what I intend.
- [ ] The cost model matches the contract.
- [ ] I know this affects only new payments.

**Never**
- Never raise a limit to make a test pass.
- Never resume a route with an open breaker without the Gateway Admin.

**If you made a mistake**
Revert the change through the normal review; pause the route if customers are harmed.
checklist: I know which rail and gateway this route joins.
Minimum, maximum and daily cap are correct and in LYD.
The credential policy and scope are what I intend.
The cost model matches the contract.
I know this affects only new payments.

cards.title: Create a draft from an AI-generated spec
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are saving the AI-generated configuration as a **draft**. Nothing goes live.

**Check first**
- [ ] The four verification layers all passed.
- [ ] I read the preview and compared it with the partner's own document.
- [ ] I typed secrets only into the platform's fields, never into the AI.
- [ ] I chose Create New or New Version deliberately.

**Never**
- Never paste a real secret into an AI.
- Never treat a passed check as approval.

**If you made a mistake**
Delete or supersede the draft; it has no effect on payments.
checklist: The four verification layers all passed.
I read the preview and compared it with the partner's own document.
I typed secrets only into the platform's fields, never into the AI.
I chose Create New or New Version deliberately.

cards.title: Run a statement file
cards.body:
**What this does**
You are matching a partner's statement against our books. Problem lines open cases.

**Check first**
- [ ] The file is the right partner, the right period and the right source.
- [ ] The preview shows columns read correctly (amount, fee, date, time zone).
- [ ] This file has not been loaded before.
- [ ] I know what to do with mismatches ([[a:b08-06]]).

**Never**
- Never edit the file to make it match.
- Never run a file from an unknown source.

**If you made a mistake**
Tell Finance. A wrong run is corrected through cases and adjustments, never by editing.
checklist: The file is the right partner, the right period and the right source.
The preview shows columns read correctly (amount, fee, date, time zone).
This file has not been loaded before.
I know what to do with mismatches ([[a:b08-06]]).

cards.title: Run a backup now
cards.body:
**What this does**
You ask the backup daemon to take a **Full** or **Delta** backup of one store or of all stores right now. It runs in the background and is queued behind any job already running.

**Check first**
- [ ] **Daemon status** says **Reachable** and the banner about an unreachable daemon is not shown.
- [ ] **Storage targets** shows every target **Healthy**.
- [ ] I know why I need it now (for example before maintenance, a configuration change or a certificate rotation).
- [ ] I chose the right **Backup target** and **Backup kind**. **All targets** with **Full** loads production, so I will do it when the platform is calm.

**Never**
- Never click **Run backup now** repeatedly to "make it go faster"; extra requests are queued behind the first.
- Never treat a started backup as finished. Wait for **Passed**.

**If you made a mistake**
A backup cannot harm data, only load the system. If you started the wrong one, let it finish and tell the Security Admin. If it ends **Failed**, read the **Error** column and see [[a:b12-10]].
checklist: **Daemon status** says **Reachable** and the banner about an unreachable daemon is not shown.
**Storage targets** shows every target **Healthy**.
I know why I need it now (for example before maintenance, a configuration change or a certificate rotation).
I chose the right **Backup target** and **Backup kind**. **All targets** with **Full** loads production, so I will do it when the platform is calm.

cards.title: Run a restore drill
cards.body:
**What this does**
You ask the daemon to restore the latest backup chain into an isolated scratch cluster, replay the archived WAL to a target time and run the three invariant checks. Production is not touched and the scratch cluster is destroyed afterwards.

**Check first**
- [ ] **Daemon status** says **Reachable**.
- [ ] I understand it can take several minutes and runs after any job already running.
- [ ] I will read the result in **Latest restore drill** and will not assume success.
- [ ] I know that a failed check is a priority-1 incident ([[s:s-restore-drill-failed]]).

**Never**
- Never ignore a **Drill failed** result because the money checks passed.
- Never delete or prune backups to make a drill pass.

**If you made a mistake**
An extra drill is harmless. If a result is red, follow [[s:s-restore-drill-failed]] at once.
checklist: **Daemon status** says **Reachable**.
I understand it can take several minutes and runs after any job already running.
I will read the result in **Latest restore drill** and will not assume success.
I know that a failed check is a priority-1 incident ([[s:s-restore-drill-failed]]).

cards.title: Change the backup schedule or retention
cards.body:
**What this does**
You propose new cron schedules (Full, Delta, Drill), retention (**Full retention days**, **WAL retention days**) or the **Alert lag threshold**. A second Security Admin must approve before anything changes.

**Check first**
- [ ] I have a written reason, for example a change of agreed recovery targets.
- [ ] Every cron expression has five fields and is in UTC.
- [ ] Retention is not lowered: shorter retention can destroy the history we need for recovery or an investigation.
- [ ] The **Alert lag threshold** is not raised just to hide a warning.
- [ ] I will ask a different Security Admin to review the `BACKUP_POLICY` request on **Approvals** ([[a:b12-11]]).

**Never**
- Never ask someone to approve a policy change without telling them what it does.
- Never use a second account of your own as the checker.

**If you made a mistake**
Before it is approved, ask for the request to be rejected and submit a corrected one. After approval, submit and approve a new change that restores the old values; the audit log keeps both.

playbook.title: A payment is stuck in UNKNOWN
playbook.body:
### What you are seeing
An attempt shows `UNKNOWN`, or the **Unknown Backlog** tile is rising.
### What it means
We did not get a clear answer from the partner. Money may or may not have moved.
### What to do
1. Check the environment badge.
2. Open the case and read the step log.
3. Press **Inquire** once.
4. If the partner cannot be asked, wait for the statement or ask the partner's support with our reference and the provider reference.
5. Resolve by hand only with evidence and a second person ([[c:sg-resolve-unknown]]).
### What not to do
Do not mark it failed because it is old. Do not ask the customer to pay again. Do not re-send an OTP.

playbook.title: A customer says money was deducted
playbook.body:
### What it means
The customer's bank or wallet shows a deduction. Our status may be anything.
### What to do
Ask for the reference, look it up and follow the table in [[a:b07-12]]. If our status is not `SUCCEEDED`, create or update a case with the reference and time.
### What not to do
Do not promise a refund. Do not say "confirmed" from a screenshot.

playbook.title: A customer cannot see a payment method
playbook.body:
### What it means
One of the nine conditions of the visible-rails formula is failing.
### What to do
Walk down the table in [[a:b06-12]]: application list, link list, commission profile, route active, route healthy, limits and daily cap, maintenance and scope, credential verified, currency and blocked flag.
### What not to do
Do not widen limits or resume a route to "make it appear".

playbook.title: A circuit breaker is open
playbook.body:
### What to do
Confirm it, tell the Gateway Admin and your manager, and let traffic move to the next route. When it closes, check the Unknown Backlog.
### What not to do
Do not re-enable the route while the partner is failing.

playbook.title: An amount is 1000 times too large or too small
playbook.body:
### What it means
The gateway's amount scale or precision is wrong.
### What to do
Stop. Treat as P1. Tell the Gateway Admin and Security Admin. Pause the route (a risk-reducing action). Do not retry payments.

playbook.title: Signature failures or webhooks from an unknown address
playbook.body:
### What to do
Follow [[a:b10-03]]. Never accept unsigned messages to get things moving.

playbook.title: A confirmation arrived after the payment expired
playbook.body:
### What to do
If the slot was free, the platform posted it and raised a P2 alert. If the link was already paid, the money is in `SUSPENSE` and a refund is drafted; Finance approves through the normal route.

playbook.title: A webhook and an inquiry disagree
playbook.body:
### What to do
Nothing was posted. This is a P1 conflict case. Escalate to a senior operator and the Gateway Admin; resolution needs partner evidence.

playbook.title: The partner's amount differs from ours
playbook.body:
### What to do
Read the route's mismatch policy result and the case. Compare with the statement. Propose any correction through Finance.

playbook.title: A statement has lines that do not match
playbook.body:
### What to do
Check the file, source and time zone. `MISSING_AT_GATEWAY` is the most serious. Never edit the file.

playbook.title: The ledger invariant shows drift
playbook.body:
### What to do
Treat as P1. Payouts stop automatically. Follow [[a:b10-05]]. Never edit numbers.

playbook.title: A merchant asks for a payout
playbook.body:
### What to do
Check the snapshot of bank details, merchant state, balance and holds. Process with a checklist; a different Finance user approves the subtraction.

playbook.title: A chargeback or dispute arrives
playbook.body:
### What to do
Check the evidence deadline. The system drafts the adjustment; a human Finance checker must approve before any money moves.

playbook.title: A refund or chargeback exceeds the merchant's balance
playbook.body:
### What to do
If it would breach the ceiling, it does not post; a P1 case opens. Finance chooses to collect, net or suspend.

playbook.title: A merchant asks why it is restricted
playbook.body:
### What to say
"Your account is currently restricted. Please contact the support address in your notice." Nothing more. Tell Compliance.

playbook.title: A screening shows a possible match
playbook.body:
### What to do
Compliance decides each match with a written rationale. Do not approve a merchant until matches are decided. Never discuss it outside Compliance.

playbook.title: An emergency suspension needs ratification
playbook.body:
### What to do
A different Compliance user or the MLRO reviews within 24 hours. If nobody does, a P2 alert fires and the suspension stays in force.

playbook.title: A join request looks like a past applicant
playbook.body:
### What to do
A second reviewer is required. Review the related records. Do not tell the applicant why.

playbook.title: A merchant says its API token leaked
playbook.body:
### What to do
The merchant revokes it in its portal and creates a new one. Never ask for the token value.

playbook.title: A credential set turned FAILING
playbook.body:
### What to do
Follow [[a:b10-06]]: replace the secret through two-person approval and run the credential check.

playbook.title: A button is missing or an action was refused
playbook.body:
### What to do
Read [[a:b03-07]]. Do not work around it.

playbook.title: An approval expired or is out of date
playbook.body:
### What to do
The maker creates a new request from the current values.

playbook.title: A POS screen went offline
playbook.body:
### What to do
The payment continues on the server. Look it up by reference.

playbook.title: The customer says the code never arrived
playbook.body:
### What to do
Ask them to wait for the countdown, check the number and use resend once.

playbook.title: I approved or proposed the wrong thing
playbook.body:
### What to do
Stop. Tell your manager. Do not edit; offset with a new approved entry.

playbook.title: I pasted a secret in the wrong place
playbook.body:
### What to do
Tell the Security Admin now. The secret must be rotated.

playbook.title: I am not sure if this is sandbox or live
playbook.body:
### What to do
Stop. Read the badge. If still unsure, ask before acting.

playbook.title: A new gateway version is misbehaving
playbook.body:
### What to do
Pause the route, then roll back to the named rollback version through the normal review.

playbook.title: The partner rejects our reference
playbook.body:
### What to do
Tell the Gateway Admin; the reference format contract test (gate 4) is the place to fix it.

playbook.title: The Backups screen says the backup daemon is unreachable
playbook.body:
### What it means
The core cannot talk to the backup daemon over mutual TLS. **Run backup now**, **Run restore drill** and **Edit policy** are disabled. Scheduled backups and WAL archiving may not be happening.

### What to do
1. Do not guess and do not try to fix servers yourself. Tell the Security Admin and the people who run the servers.
2. Ask them to check that the backup daemon service is running on its host, that its certificate and the core's backup client certificate are valid, and that the network path from the core to the daemon is open.
3. Remember that the database keeps WAL segments it has not yet delivered. A long outage can fill the database disk, so do not leave this overnight.
4. When **Daemon status** returns to **Reachable**, press **Refresh**, confirm **WAL archive lag** drains and check **Last backup**. If a scheduled backup was missed, a Security Admin can run a **Delta** ([[c:sg-trigger-backup]]).

playbook.title: WAL archive lag is Attention or Critical
playbook.body:
### What it means
**Attention** means the lag is above the **Alert threshold** (default 300 s). **Critical** means above twice the threshold. Recent changes are not yet safely archived, so a disaster now would lose more than a few seconds.

### What to do
1. Read **Archive lag**, **Lag bytes**, **Current LSN** and **Last archived LSN**. Press **Refresh** twice a minute apart: is the lag falling or growing?
2. Open **Storage targets** and **Daemon status**. A **Failed** target (for example the S3 or MinIO bucket) or an **Unreachable** daemon is the usual cause. See [[s:s-backup-daemon-unreachable]].
3. Tell the Security Admin and the people who run the servers. Until archiving catches up, WAL piles up on the database disk.
4. Do not raise the **Alert lag threshold** to silence the warning.
5. Confirm recovery: **Archive lag** back under the threshold and the tile **Healthy**.

playbook.title: A restore drill failed
playbook.body:
### What it means
Any failed check is a **priority-1 incident**. Read the three badges in **Latest restore drill**.

### What to do
1. **Double-entry zero drift** or **Sharded balance parity** failed: tell Finance and the Security Admin. Open **Ledger Audit & Invariant** under **Finance** to see whether production also drifts, then follow RB-04 ([[a:b10-05]], [[a:b08-05]]).
2. **Audit hash chain** failed: escalate immediately to the Security Admin. Do not delete, prune or alter any backup, and do not touch audit records.
3. **Drill failed** with a red error text and no failed check (the backup could not be fetched or the scratch cluster did not start): we have no proof that recovery works. Ask the people who run the servers to fix the cause, then run another drill ([[c:sg-run-restore-drill]]) and confirm all three badges read **Passed**.
4. Write down the drill id, the time and what you saw, in the incident record.

paths.title: New employee: day one to day five

faq.question: What does UNKNOWN mean?
faq.answer: We asked the payment company to take money and did not get a clear answer. We do not know whether money moved. Do not guess: press Inquire, then follow the UNKNOWN article.

faq.question: Can I mark an old UNKNOWN as failed?
faq.answer: No. Age is not evidence. Resolve it by hand only with evidence from the partner (a statement line or a written reply) and a second person.

faq.question: A customer says they paid but I see FAILED. What do I say?
faq.answer: Say you have no confirmed payment. Ask them to keep their receipt and reference, and not to pay again. Open a case. A late confirmation may still arrive.

faq.question: Should I ask the customer to pay again?
faq.answer: No. If the first payment actually succeeded they would pay twice.

faq.question: Can I confirm a payment from a screenshot?
faq.answer: No. Only a status you read in the platform counts. Screens on customers' phones can be faked.

faq.question: What if the partner has no status question?
faq.answer: The screen will say an inquiry is not possible. Wait for the next statement, or ask the partner's support with our reference and the provider reference.

faq.question: Why can't another customer pay a single-use link while one payment is unknown?
faq.answer: The first payment might have succeeded. The slot stays reserved so one invoice cannot be paid twice.

faq.question: How many wrong OTP tries are allowed?
faq.answer: Three by default. The third wrong code fails the payment.

faq.question: What is a late success?
faq.answer: A confirmation that arrives after the payment expired or failed. If the slot is free it is posted; if the link was already paid, the money is parked in SUSPENSE and a refund is drafted.

faq.question: What happens when a webhook and an inquiry disagree?
faq.answer: Nothing is posted, the payment stays UNKNOWN and a priority-1 conflict case opens.

faq.question: Why do amounts have three decimals?
faq.answer: One dinar is 1000 dirhams. Some partners use two decimals or whole dirhams, so the amount settings must be exact or the amount is 1000 times wrong.

faq.question: A customer was asked for 1000 times the amount. What now?
faq.answer: Stop, treat it as P1, tell the Gateway Admin and Security Admin, pause the route and do not retry.

faq.question: Why does a customer not see a payment method?
faq.answer: One of the nine visible-rails conditions fails. Walk down the table to find the first one.

faq.question: What is a circuit breaker?
faq.answer: An automatic switch-off of a failing route. Customers stop seeing it and new payments use the next route. Only partner faults count, not customer mistakes.

faq.question: Can I edit a live gateway?
faq.answer: No. Editing creates a new draft version. The live version stays untouched until the new one is approved and promoted.

faq.question: Can I paste the partner's secret key into the AI?
faq.answer: Never. Give the AI only the names of the credentials. Type the real secrets into the platform afterwards.

faq.question: Does an AI-generated spec go live automatically?
faq.answer: No. It arrives as a draft with a paused route and an untested credential set. It still needs the credential check, the 12 gates and a second person.

faq.question: How many go-live gates are there?
faq.answer: Twelve. A version cannot go live until all pass.

faq.question: Why do signatures fail?
faq.answer: Usually the key encoding, the field order or set, or the upper or lower case of the result.

faq.question: Can an administrator read a stored secret?
faq.answer: No. Secrets are write-only: you can replace them but never read them back.

faq.question: Why must a second person approve?
faq.answer: It catches honest mistakes, prevents one person acting alone, and creates a clear record of who proposed and who approved.

faq.question: How long does an approval request last?
faq.answer: Seven days. After that it returns to draft and the maker must re-submit.

faq.question: The system says Forbidden. What do I do?
faq.answer: The core refused: role, authority or the two-person rule. Do not retry or work around it. Ask your manager or the Security Admin.

faq.question: What is the difference between descriptive and sensitive fields?
faq.answer: Descriptive fields (for example a trade name) are edited directly. Sensitive fields change money flow, compliance or attack surface and need two people.

faq.question: What is an emergency suspension?
faq.answer: One authorised person suspends a merchant at once. A different Compliance user or the MLRO must ratify it within 24 hours. It stays in force if nobody does.

faq.question: What makes a good reason?
faq.answer: What you checked, what you found, what you decided and why, written so a stranger can understand it months later.

faq.question: How many checks does a join request review need?
faq.answer: Seven. All must be completed and recorded.

faq.question: When does a second reviewer have to approve a join request?
faq.answer: When the platform setting requires it. The default risk-based policy requires it for high risk, an unclear screening result, a politically exposed owner, a high-risk category, high volume, a payout account mismatch or a previous rejection.

faq.question: Why does an application have exactly one wallet?
faq.answer: So a payment can never be ambiguous about where its money goes.

faq.question: Can I see a merchant's API token?
faq.answer: No. It is shown once to the merchant when created. Never ask for it.

faq.question: What happens when a merchant is suspended?
faq.answer: New payments and cash-outs are blocked, tokens and POS screens return a neutral message, and the balance is kept.

faq.question: A merchant asks why it was restricted. What do I say?
faq.answer: Say only that the account is restricted and to contact the support address in the notice. Never mention compliance or investigation.

faq.question: What does double-entry mean?
faq.answer: Every movement is written on two sides that must add up. If they do not, the system refuses the entry.

faq.question: Can a ledger entry be edited?
faq.answer: No. The ledger is append-only. A mistake is corrected by a new approved entry that offsets it.

faq.question: How many kinds of GL account are there?
faq.answer: Eleven.

faq.question: What is the difference between commission and gateway fee?
faq.answer: Commission is what we charge the merchant. Gateway fee is what the payment company charges us.

faq.question: What does ledger drift mean?
faq.answer: The two sides of the ledger equation differ. It must always be zero. Any drift is a priority-1 incident and automatic payouts stop.

faq.question: What is MISSING_AT_GATEWAY?
faq.answer: We say a payment succeeded but the partner's statement does not show it. This is the most serious reconciliation result.

faq.question: Who approves the subtraction of a cash-out?
faq.answer: A different Finance user from the one who processed it.

faq.question: How do I fix a wrong adjustment?
faq.answer: Never edit it. Propose a new adjustment that offsets it, which also needs approval.

faq.question: Who approves a chargeback?
faq.answer: A human Finance checker. The system may draft it but can never approve it.

faq.question: What if a chargeback is bigger than the merchant's balance?
faq.answer: If it would pass the merchant's negative-balance ceiling it does not post and a priority-1 case opens. Finance chooses to collect, net or suspend.

faq.question: What is money laundering?
faq.answer: Making money from crime look like it came from a legitimate source, usually through placement, layering and integration.

faq.question: What is tipping-off?
faq.answer: Telling someone, directly or by hint, that they are under suspicion or that a report exists. It is forbidden and can be a crime.

faq.question: May Support see why a merchant is suspended?
faq.answer: No. Support can see that a merchant is suspended, never why.

faq.question: What happens on a possible screening match?
faq.answer: A Compliance analyst decides each match. An applicant cannot be approved until then.

faq.question: Who approves an AML case resolution?
faq.answer: The MLRO, never the same person as the analyst who proposed it. Money moves only after approval.

faq.question: Can we file a report from a provisional rule?
faq.answer: No. The database refuses it. Until the Central Bank's requirements are confirmed the platform works in internal-only mode.

faq.question: I think something is suspicious. What do I do?
faq.answer: Do not confront anyone. Write down the facts and tell Compliance the same day. Keep it confidential.

faq.question: Which runbook do I use?
faq.answer: Use the table in the incident principles article: breaker for outages, RB-02 for signatures, RB-03 for UNKNOWN backlog, RB-04 for drift, RB-05 for credentials.

faq.question: Why did payouts stop?
faq.answer: The ledger equation shows drift. Automatic payouts stop until the cause is understood and the drift is zero.

faq.question: I think my password leaked. What now?
faq.answer: Tell the Security Admin immediately and change your password from a clean device. Do not wait to be sure.

faq.question: Can I share my login with a colleague who is locked out?
faq.answer: Never. Ask the Security Admin.

faq.question: Why can't I open the Back Office from home?
faq.answer: It is LAN-only by design. It is not reachable from the internet.

faq.question: What is Fake Rails?
faq.answer: Our internal service that imitates payment companies for drills. It must never run in production.

faq.question: What is the difference between sandbox and live?
faq.answer: Sandbox is a practice world; nothing real moves. Live is real money. Always check the badge before acting.

faq.question: What if the guide and the screen disagree?
faq.answer: Stop and ask. Use Report a problem on the article.

faq.question: What are the most serious breaches?
faq.answer: Sharing credentials, guessing on UNKNOWN and tipping-off.
